title: Finite affine fppf covers have vanishing quasi-coherent Cech cohomology
statement: Fix the universes and small site presentations of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ an arbitrary quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $F^a$ its associated module sheaf on $\mathcal C_S=(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-scheme-big-fppf-quasicoherent-equivalence]. Thus $F^a(v:T\to S)=\Gamma(T,v^*F)$ with tensor-pullback restrictions [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $u:V\to S$ be an object with $V$ affine, and let $\mathcal V=\{g_i:V_i\to V\}_{i\in I}$ be an fppf covering with $I$ finite and every $V_i$ affine. For the underlying abelian sheaf $(F^a)_{ab}$, form the Cech complex of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex], whose degree $p\ge0$ term is $\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}}\Gamma(V_{i_0}\times_V\cdots\times_V V_{i_p},(u g_{i_0}\operatorname{pr}_0)^*F)$ and whose differential is the alternating sum of restriction along projections omitting one factor. Then $\check H^p(\mathcal V,(F^a)_{ab})=0$ for every $p>0$. The empty covering of the empty affine scheme and empty covering members are allowed. No finite-generation or flatness hypothesis on $F$, and no Noetherian or separation hypothesis on $S$, is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03FJ, lemma-standard-covering-Cech-quasi-coherent, fppf case (with the standard finite affine coverings of Tag 03FI, lemma-standard-covering-Cech).

proof.text: Put $G=u^*F$ and $M=\Gamma(V,G)$. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence, so $G$ is quasi-coherent on the affine scheme $V$. The base-restriction clause of the big-fppf equivalence identifies $F^a|_{(\mathit{Sch}/V)_{\mathrm{fppf}}}$ with $A_V(G)$, whose value on $w:T\to V$ is $\Gamma(T,w^*G)$ and whose restrictions are tensor pullbacks. Thus we may compute the displayed Cech complex using $G$ on $V$. This is the canonical composite-pullback identification, not any exactness assertion about the associated-sheaf functor.

source.place: Tag 03FJ, proof: set R=Gamma(U,O_U), M=Gamma(U,F^a); Tag 03LC (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent-functorial)(1), restriction to the base object.

proof.text: Write $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, $A_i=\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal O_{V_i})$, and $B=\prod_{i\in I}A_i$ with its diagonal $A$-algebra structure. Each $g_i$ is flat by the fppf-cover definition, hence $A\to A_i$ is flat by the affine criterion. The finite product lemma makes $B$ flat over $A$. The finite-coproduct spectrum isomorphism identifies $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $\coprod_i V_i$, compatibly with the coordinate maps to $V$. Every point of $V$ lifts to some $V_i$ by joint surjectivity, and then to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ by its coprojection. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is surjective. The flat-surjective spectrum criterion gives faithful flatness of $A\to B$.

source.place: Tags 03FI and 03FJ, proof: replace the finite affine family by its coproduct and obtain a faithfully flat coordinate algebra; Morphisms 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize), Algebra 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings).

proof.text:
For a tuple $\mathbf i=(i_0,\ldots,i_p)$, put $T_{\mathbf i}=V_{i_0}\times_V\cdots\times_V V_{i_p}$ and $w_{\mathbf i}:T_{\mathbf i}\to V$. Inductively applying the affine fibre-product theorem identifies $T_{\mathbf i}$ with $\operatorname{Spec}D_{\mathbf i}$, where $D_{\mathbf i}=A_{i_0}\otimes_A\cdots\otimes_A A_{i_p}$. Its projection omitting factor $j$ corresponds to the algebra map inserting $1$ in slot $j$: both maps agree on each retained factor by the stated projection formulas and the tensor universal property. The affine-section theorem, applied with the whole source and target as affine opens, gives the isomorphism
$$c_{\mathbf i}:M\otimes_A D_{\mathbf i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T_{\mathbf i},w_{\mathbf i}^*G),\qquad m\otimes d\longmapsto d\,w_{\mathbf i}^*m.$$
No affine-open intersections in $S$ are used.

source.place: Tag 03FJ, displayed calculation of the degree p term; Schemes 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines), 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback).

proof.text:
For every $p\ge0$, repeated application of the finite-product tensor isomorphism, with tensor-factor associativity and symmetry, gives
$$M\otimes_A B^{\otimes_A(p+1)}\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{\mathbf i\in I^{p+1}}(M\otimes_A D_{\mathbf i}).$$
There are only finitely many factors at each application, and the other tensor factor may be an arbitrary module. Compose with $\prod_{\mathbf i}c_{\mathbf i}$ to obtain $\alpha_p:M\otimes_A B^{\otimes_A(p+1)}\xrightarrow{\sim}C^p$, where $C^p$ is the Cech term. Explicitly, for $b^r=(b^r_i)_{i\in I}\in B$,
$$\bigl(\alpha_p(m\otimes b^0\otimes\cdots\otimes b^p)\bigr)_{\mathbf i}=c_{\mathbf i}(m\otimes b^0_{i_0}\otimes\cdots\otimes b^p_{i_p}).$$
This is a composition of the cited isomorphisms; no new existence or comparison theorem is assumed.

source.place: Tags 03FI and 03FJ, degreewise comparison with the coproduct and tensor-power cochains; Algebra 00DD (lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits), finite products equal finite direct sums.

proof.text:
Check each coface, not just the degreewise terms. Let $\mathbf k=(k_0,\ldots,k_{p+1})$ and let $\pi_j:T_{\mathbf k}\to T_{\mathbf k\setminus j}$ omit factor $j$. Under the ring coordinates of step 3, its pullback takes
$$m\otimes a_0\otimes\cdots\otimes a_p\longmapsto m\otimes a_0\otimes\cdots\otimes a_{j-1}\otimes1\otimes a_j\otimes\cdots\otimes a_p.$$
Indeed, pull back the section $d\,w^*m$ in the formula for $c$: it becomes $\pi_j^\sharp(d)\,(w\pi_j)^*m$, by the tensor-pullback definition and the canonical composite identification. The insertion of $1_B$ on $M\otimes_A B^{\otimes_A(p+1)}$ has component $1_{A_{k_j}}$, so step 4 gives exactly this same section in component $\mathbf k$. Pure tensors generate the source as an abelian group, so the two homomorphisms agree. Summing over $j$ with signs $(-1)^j$ proves $d_C^p\alpha_p=\alpha_{p+1}d_{\mathrm{Am}}^p$. Thus the $\alpha_p$ form an isomorphism of cochain complexes, with the alternating Amitsur differential.

source.place: Tag 03FJ, sentence omitting verification of the Cech maps; the verification here uses the explicit section map of Schemes 01I9 and the composite-pullback isomorphism of Sheaves 0097 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules).

proof.text: Apply the augmented Amitsur exactness theorem to the faithfully flat $A$-algebra $B$ of step 2 and the arbitrary $A$-module $M$. In every degree $p>0$, it says $\ker d_{\mathrm{Am}}^p=\operatorname{im}d_{\mathrm{Am}}^{p-1}$. The complex isomorphism of step 5 carries these kernels and images onto those of $C^\bullet$. The definition $\check H^p=\ker d_C^p/\operatorname{im}d_C^{p-1}$ therefore gives the required zero group. This does not require $M$ flat or finitely generated. If $I=\varnothing$, the covering condition forces $V=\varnothing$, and every $C^p$ is the empty product of abelian groups, hence zero; the result follows directly. Empty members in a nonempty family have $A_i=0$; all the finite-product, affine-spectrum and tensor isomorphisms above still apply. No separation or Noetherian hypothesis was used.
